script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: “Keep your sheep” adds an instruction Jacob does not give.
The passage does not say the tents stayed packed. Marking that as a guess does not establish what happened to them.
Jacob says they are going to Bethel so he can build an altar; he does not say they are going there to meet God.
“Nobody's reaching for a razor” asserts an action the passage does not describe.
The passage does not say Jacob had an armful of items or needed a larger sack.
The passage does not say everyone kept their footwear and walked to Bethel in it.
The passage does not say the people kept leaning on their staffs.
The statement that they were camped by Shechem comes from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not say Jacob took a deep breath. It allows a marked guess about a feeling, not an invented action.
The verse does not describe the sky, so it does not establish that they walked under clear skies.
The text says the surrounding cities did not pursue Jacob's sons; it does not say everyone in those cities stayed put.
The passage does not say the road to Bethel stayed quiet.
Jacob names the place El-bethel, not the altar.
The explanation is mechanical: after the quotation, both sentences simply repeat that the word is kings.
This is a generic restatement of the answer, with no distinct Papa Dorin voice or further explanation.

The passage says God gave the land to Abraham and Isaac and will give it to Jacob and his descendants. It does not say a promise to Abraham and Isaac now passes to Jacob; that claim needs support from the relevant passages.
The passage says God will give the land to Jacob; it does not say the land is passed down to him from Abraham and Isaac.
The explanation is flat and generic, ending with two bare observations about the answer's position in the verse.
The text does not establish that anyone walking by would know something happened at the pillar.
The final sentence guesses why the midwife spoke. Her unstated motive should not be added, even as a guess.
The text says Jacob returned to Isaac at Mamre, not that Jacob was home or that his long journey had finally ended.
